title: Illinois eBike Regulations
seo_title: Illinois eBike Regulations & Ottawa Rules | Quest
seo_description: Where can you ride an eBike in Ottawa, IL? City rules today and Illinois SB 3484 starting January 1, 2027, plus Class 1, 2 and 3 explained by Quest Watersports.
body_html:
Illinois Senate Bill 3484 passed the General Assembly in June 2026 and awaits the Governor's expected signature. The new statewide rules take effect January 1, 2027, not July 1, 2026 as some reports claimed. Here is what changes and what stays the same for Ottawa-area riders.

The rules today: City of Ottawa ordinance (2025)

  • Where you can ride: city streets posted 25 mph or less. Riding around Heritage Harbor's streets is legal today.
  • Off-limits: streets over 25 mph, LaSalle Street in the downtown business district, sidewalks, city parks and other public property.
  • Minimum age: 16 for all eBike classes (Class 1, 2 and 3).
  • No driver's license required for Class 1 to 3 eBikes.
  • Motors 750 watts and up are prohibited everywhere in the city: streets, paths and parking lots.
  • Violations: fines of $75 to $750 and possible impoundment by Ottawa PD.

Starting January 1, 2027: Illinois state law (SB 3484)

  • Where you can ride: Class 1 to 3 eBikes are treated like bicycles statewide. Ride wherever bicycles are allowed: streets, bike lanes and bike paths. Ottawa's 25-mph street limit, downtown ban and parks ban go away.
  • Still off-limits: sidewalks and interstate-type highways, same as any bicycle. State agencies and park districts can set rules for their own trails.
  • Minimum age: 15 for Class 1 and 2; 16 for Class 3.
  • Still no license, registration or insurance for Class 1 to 3 eBikes.
  • Motors over 750 watts become "motor driven cycles": driver's license, insurance and title required, and banned from all bike lanes, paths and trails.
  • One statewide rulebook: local eBike ordinances no longer apply. The same rules cover Ottawa, Utica and everywhere in between.

How to tell what you have

Every legal low-speed eBike has a permanent label on the frame listing its class number, top assisted speed and motor wattage.

  • Class 1: pedal assist up to 20 mph
  • Class 2: throttle up to 20 mph
  • Class 3: pedal assist up to 28 mph

If a bike has no label, or the seller cannot tell you its class, it may be a "motor driven cycle" that requires a license, insurance and a title starting in 2027, and cannot be ridden on trails.

Questions?

Questions about eBike classes, the new law or what is right for your rides? Quest Watersports is happy to help, with no pressure. Call (815) 433-2200 or email us. Ready to ride? See our eBikes, eBike rentals and the I&M Canal Trail guide.

For general information only, not legal advice. Summarizes City of Ottawa Ordinance Sec. 86-18/86-19 and Illinois SB 3484 as passed June 2026.

faqs.q: What is the minimum age to ride an eBike in Ottawa today?
faqs.a: 16 for all eBike classes under the 2025 City of Ottawa ordinance. Starting January 1, 2027, state law sets 15 for Class 1 and 2 and 16 for Class 3.

faqs.q: Where can I ride an eBike in Ottawa today?
faqs.a: On city streets posted 25 mph or less, including the streets around Heritage Harbor. Streets over 25 mph, LaSalle Street downtown, sidewalks, city parks and other public property are off-limits.

faqs.q: Do I need a license, registration or insurance for an eBike?
faqs.a: Not for Class 1 to 3 eBikes, today or under the 2027 state law. Motors over 750 watts become motor driven cycles in 2027 and require a license, insurance and title.
Class 1 to 3 eBikes are treated like bicycles statewide, so you can ride wherever bicycles are allowed. Local eBike ordinances no longer apply.

faqs.q: How do I know my eBike's class?
faqs.a: Look for the permanent frame label showing class, top assisted speed and motor wattage. Class 1 is pedal assist to 20 mph, Class 2 is throttle to 20 mph, Class 3 is pedal assist to 28 mph.

faqs.q: What are the penalties for violating Ottawa's ordinance?
faqs.a: Fines of $75 to $750 and possible impoundment by Ottawa PD.
